newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse sets new record, stable week ahead.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse sets new record, stable week ahead.

text.p: Belgium's blue-chip index, which set a record close on Friday helped again by a higher New York market and a strong dollar, was expected to hover at this level in the coming week as fundamentals remained in order.
"We should be able to maintain the 2,000 level if the dollar remains at this level," said trader Benoit Kint at brokerage Petercam.
The Bel-20 closed up 0.41 percent, or 8.23 points, at 2,006.79, after touching a historical intraday high of 2,010.67.
"There are not many sellers, it's kind of neutral and this is why we didn't have much profit-taking," said Kint.
Dealers said a period of consolidation would help the market and avoid any major correction later on in the year.
"I prefer to have a small consolidation (period) instead of having a sharp correction in five months' time," said analyst Gert De Mesure at Bank Delen.
"I have the same problem everyday, I have too much liquidity," said one trader.
Thursday's main Bel-20 gainer, non-ferrous metals producer Union Miniere, failed to hold its own, despite the dollar's strength and higher zinc prices. It ended down 1.17 percent at 2,300 francs.
"The market exaggerated yesterday on Union Miniere as zinc price rises were not high enough to justify Union Miniere's rise," said Kint.
Another trader felt Union Miniere could rise again.
"I'm confident it will go up further, but there's resistance between 2,300 (francs) and 2,400, but if it breaks 2,400 then it's free to go up".
Analyst Gert De Mesure said, "there's a lot of foreign investors who have built up positions in Union Miniere, especially Dutch investors".
Bel-20's leading climber was insurance group Fortis AG, closing up 1,27 percent at 5,600 francs.
Dealers said this was a correction after Thursday's profit-taking after AG announced that it planned to raise 17 billion Belgian francs to pay for recent acquisitions.
